card.title: How To Read and Write iPhone 16 Pro SPI EEPROM using CH341A

source.title: How To Read and Write iPhone 16 Pro SPI EEPROM using CH341A

claims.statement: iPhone 16 Pro charging faults can come from corrupted ACE charging-controller EEPROM data (after bad chargers or surges); replacing the ACE controller alone does not fix it.
The ACE SPI EEPROM can be read and rewritten in-circuit with a CH341A via jumper wires, avoiding a sandwich split and preserving data.

procedure: Inspect around the ACE controller and ROM.
Check USB-C negotiation on a meter.
Remove power; jumper CH341A to the ACE SPI points.
Detect, read twice, save two copies and compare.
Program a good image and verify; remove jumpers, test charging.
card.caveats: Source of a known-good EEPROM image is not specified. Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
